A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LEGATO research and provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures. v1 ends with references; v2 adds Appendices A-B containing both relocated and new material. The complete documents support comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Table 1 report original LEGATO experiments on PDMX-Synth, OpenScore datasets, and manually annotated IMSLP piano scores, including comparisons with SMT++.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds GPT-5 benchmark results and qualitative piano transcription experiments in Appendix B.3.

M1.justification: The frozen Llama vision encoder, image segmentation, 4,097-item BPE vocabulary, projector, decoder architectures, and next-token training procedure are unchanged. Highlighting tokenization as an explicit contribution does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: The training data and quantitative benchmark coverage are retained. Appendix B.3 adds selected piano excerpts outside the evaluation dataset, including an explicitly context-deficient Liszt example with omitted triplet and rest notation. This modestly extends the tested input conditions.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds GPT-5 alongside SMT++ across camera and rendered Quartets, camera and rendered Lieder, and IMSLP Piano Scores. This substantially broadens comparison from a specialized OMR baseline to a general-purpose multimodal model. The violin-only comparison retains its original comparator set in Table 2.

E3.justification: The added GPT-5 evaluation uses an explicit prompt requesting ABC output despite uncertainty. Figure 6 introduces isolated-system inputs and system-level TEDn evaluation. Existing LEGATO training budgets, decoding settings, benchmark sample sizes, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B.3 and Figure 6 add Mozart, Chopin, and Liszt case studies examining font and slur recognition, scan artifacts, and missing contextual notation. The existing violin-only control, aspect-ratio analysis, and Bach example are retained through relocation; no new controlled ablation is introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests for its comparisons. Appendix A.1's new mention of SMT++'s five-fold cross-validation describes prior work, not additional uncertainty estimation for the reported experiments.

E6.justification: v2 adds GPT-5 results across five benchmark settings, showing lower TEDn but higher OMR-NED than SMT++; its IMSLP values are 96.7 and 98.7, respectively. Figure 6 adds further transcription outcomes and TEDn scores. Matched LEGATO and SMT++ benchmark values are unchanged, including the relocated violin results. v1's explicit 92.9% and 88.8% SMT++ MusicXML conversion-failure rates are omitted.

T1.justification: The architecture's tensor definitions and the metric definitions and complexity statements in Sections 4-5 remain unchanged. Neither version presents additional theoretical propositions, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The introduction promotes the existing finding about BPE learning composite musical concepts into an explicit contribution. The abstract now quantifies the retained IMSLP advantage as 68 and 47.6 percentage points on TEDn and OMR-NED. The principal novelty, generalization, and state-of-the-art claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking font and slur recognition to training diversity, explains failures when excerpts omit tuplet context, and tentatively attributes GPT-5's metric-dependent ranking to syntax correction. It also expands discussion of SMT++ checkpoint and evaluation limitations and adds a Markdown interoperability rationale for ABC.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly documents SMT++ checkpoint selection and decoding sources, plus the GPT-5 snapshot gpt-5-2025-08-07 and its full prompt. These are disclosures rather than evidence that existing experiments changed. The SMT++ identifier is inconsistent: smtpp_mozarteum is listed, but smtpp_kmozarteum is named as selected. Existing training details and code access remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds OpenAI's GPT-5 report and Rink's work associated with Mozarteum, positions LEGATO against general-purpose multimodal models, and expands criticism of SMT++ evaluation practices. The broader related-work discussion and original novelty positioning are retained.

P1.justification: The empirical narrative is substantially reorganized: numbered dataset subsections become compact headed paragraphs, while the focused violin comparison, multi-page analysis, and qualitative discussion move into Appendix B. Appendix A adds a separate baseline-settings section. The abstract and contribution list are revised, although most method and metric prose remains.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a GPT-5 column and expanded caption, while its violin-only block becomes Appendix Table 2. Figures 4 and 5 move to the appendix, and a new three-panel Figure 6 presents additional piano examples. Together these substantially reorganize and expand the experimental displays.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the GPT-5 comparison broadens empirical context, the disclosed prompt improves reproducibility, and the new cases clarify practical strengths and failure conditions. These provide a modest overall gain. The added robustness evidence remains illustrative, and benefits are partly offset by the inconsistent SMT++ checkpoint identifier and removal of precise conversion-failure rates; the core method and existing benchmark results are unchanged.
